key_insight: A split-head Quantum GAN separates lattice and atomic-coordinate generation to improve crystalline material discovery, with quantum features boosting structural diversity while architectural priors improve precision.
engineering_relevance: For computational materials design, the approach suggests a resource-efficient way to reduce mode collapse and generate more diverse, physically plausible crystal candidates on near-term hardware.
method: Split the generator into separate heads for macroscopic cell bounds and microscopic atomic coordinates.
Use a quantum trunk for feature mapping and compare against an architecture-matched classical ablation.
Evaluate on the constrained Mg-Mn-O composition space to test validity, diversity, and stoichiometric convergence.
evidence_signal: In the Mg-Mn-O experiments, the classical ablation was more thermodynamically precise, while SH-QGAN more than doubled geometric validity and produced novel metastable candidates near Mg2MnO4.
watch_item: Quantum gains appear complementary rather than universal, and performance may depend strongly on the target chemistry, constraint design, and hardware noise.
paper_title: Split-Head Quantum Generative Adversarial Network for Crystalline Material Discovery
